posts.title: The Pogo Pass Added the Ice Den, Wazee's World, ASU Baseball and Softball, and More to the Already Great Passes!
posts.excerpt: Spring Break is already here for some valley kids and it's close for many others! The Pogo Pass will help your family get out and have fun at places throughout…
posts.text:
Spring Break is already here for some valley kids and it's close for many others! The Pogo Pass will help your family get out and have fun at places throughout the valley for the ENTIRE YEAR (including spring break). You can head over here to get one for $49.98, usually $124.95 with code ALICIA. If you've been following my blog for awhile, you already know that the Pogo Pass is the #1 Alicia's Deal of all time and I hear from so many readers how much fun their families have with it. Pogo Pass is A+ rated with the better business bureau.
They have added new venues to make the passes an even better value (the venues change from time to time and the value is incredible). Check out what's new with your pass:  Ice Den Scottsdale/Chandler: One free skate per month during regularly scheduled public skate times. This is usually $9 for adults, skate rental is not included.  Wazees World in Peoria: Two visits per year. Choose laser tag (usually $9) or cosmic golf (usually $5).  ASU Sun Devil Athletics: Now you can get into ASU Baseball games, gymnastics meets, soccer games, women's basketball games, volleyball games, track and field meets, select softball games, and more with your pass. There are so many games to choose from and this is perfect for the budding sports star who would love to play in college (or for anyone who likes to watch sports)! Places you can still use your passes (subject to change):  Phoenix Zoo: You'll enjoy two admissions per year. Since each admission for adults is usually $24.95, this will pay for your pass by itself!  Sunsplash: You'll enjoy one general admission to Sunsplash. This is usually $35.99!  Arizona Diamondbacks: You'll enjoy seats at two select Arizona Diamondbacks games per year. Choose from Saturday, May 13 vs. Pittsburg Pirates 5:10 PM, Friday, June 23 vs. Philadelphia Phillies 6:40 PM, Friday, July 21 vs. Washington Nationals 6:40 PM, Monday, August 14 vs. Houston Astros 6:40 PM, or Friday, September 22 vs. Miami Marlins 6:40 PM. *The registration button for tickets will appear on this page (2) weeks prior to game day, and close 48 hours prior to the event to allow for tickets to be generated. You must register your Pogo Pass to receive a ticket. Tickets for the Dbacks games are picked up at will call on game day.  AZ Airtime: Two (2) visits to AZ Air Time for a One (1) hour jump session. Visits can be used at either of the two locations. Simply present your Pogo Pass at front desk for admission. One hour is usually $14, good Monday-Friday but holidays and special offers excluded (you may want to call ahead before you make a special trip). Must have non slip socks. Phoenix Rock Gym: You'll enjoy two admissions per year. Normal price is $15, gear is available to rent for $5. Skateland: Passholders will get 2 visits a month (skate rental not included)! This is good during normal business hours. Family skate is usually $7.50/person. Fat Cats: Passholders will get one game of glow golf per week and one game of bowling per month (shoe rental not included). The IDEA Museum: Passholders will get two visits to the museum (must be used by the passholder on different days). Admission is usually $8. Arizona Rattlers: *One (1) ticket per game for Three (3) Arizona Rattlers home games. Saturday, March 11 vs Colorado Crush 6:00 PM, Saturday, April 22 vs. Spokane Empire 6:00 PM, or Saturday, May 20 vs. Salt Lake Screaming Eagles 6:00 PM. *The registration button for tickets will appear on this page (2) weeks prior to game day, and close 48 hours prior to the event to allow for tickets to be generated. You must register your Pogo Pass to receive a ticket. Tickets for the Rattlers games are electronic, and will arrive via email in the days leading up to the game. Phoenix Mercury: *One (1) ticket per game, for Three (3) Phoenix Mercury home games. Saturday, May 27th vs. Dallas Wings 7:00 PM, Friday, June 30th vs. Minnesota Lynx 7:00 PM, Friday, July 14th vs. Minnesota Lynx 7:00 PM, or Thursday, Aug 24th vs. LA Sparks 6:00 PM. *The registration button for tickets will appear on this page (2) weeks prior to game day, and close 48 hoursprior to the event to allow for tickets to be generated. You must register your Pogo Pass to receive a ticket. Tickets for the Mercury games are electronic, and will arrive via email in the days leading up to the game. Tempe Paintball: *Each Pogo Pass member can attend (1) Visit to Tempe Paintball per month for Paintball or Nerf Wars. Reservations are required for both Paintball and Nerf Wars. Enchanted Island: Your Pogo Pass is good for two (2) visits to Enchanted Island Amusement Park for an All-Day Ride Pass. Admission to the park is free. Limited capacity, first come first serve. Some rides may require additional charge. An all day ride pass is usually $18.75. Stratum Laser Tag: Pogo Pass holders can attend Stratum Laser Tag two (2) separate times, Pogo Passes may be used on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays from 4:30-8pm. Regular price for one game is $9.99. COMING SOON: Urban Jungle Fun Park Things to know about the Pogo Pass: You can renew each year at a discounted rate and you'll automatically get the available venues for another year (they'll contact you a couple of weeks before your pass expires and let them know if you choose not to renew). Venues may change and passholders will be notified. As new venues are added, your pass will automatically include them. Each person in the family needs their own pass. You can do a fundraiser with Pogo Pass and make extra cash for your organization! Contact me at alicia@dealsinaz.com for more information. These will hopefully get you out and having more fun in our valley of the sun! Enjoy!

Ballet Arizona performs the most famous love story of all time just in time for Valentine's Day. Two families, the Montagues and the Capulets, have been feuding for years. But when young Romeo Montague goes out with his friends to stir up trouble at a party thrown by the Capulets, he spies Juliet, the Capulets' daughter, and falls hopelessly in love. Will love conquer all? Or will these two young lovers get caught in the crossfire of their family's bloody feud? With its sweepingly regal ballroom scenes, vivacious swordplay and poignant pas de deux, Ib Andersen's production is a feast for the eyes, ears and heart. See it at Phoenix Symphony Hall."

"The entire excursion lasts about 3.5 hours. Guests arrive in time to watch the balloon inflate as the sun rises. Then, pilots propel as many as 12 passengers through clear blue skies for up to 60 minutes as they take in the picturesque views.
Afterward, guests are treated to a commemorative flight certificate, a champagne toast, and a light snack, over which the crew discusses the history of hot-air balloons.
The company’s year-round balloon flights depart at sunrise, toting riders into the sky over the valley with seasoned pilots at the helm. Occasionally, flights can rise to a high enough altitude to allow sightseers to glimpse locales as far as Sedona or the San Francisco peaks at the base of the Colorado Plateau. The Praise: Chicago’s Robert Lamm calls the tour “The perfect summer lineup,” sharing he’s “happy to be hangin’ out with our Doobie friends,” and The Doobie Brothers’ Tom Johnston declares, “We are so excited to once again be sharing the stage with our wonderful friends Chicago! Benefits
This machine is designed to create smooth, uniform curls without the strain and fuss of twisting a traditional curling iron.
How It Works
Hair is drawn into a ceramic curl chamber, where it’s coiled and heated up until each curl is set. Users can choose to release the hair on their own or opt for a pre-set timer that beeps when it’s time to set hair free after creating a loose wave, soft curl, or more-defined curl.
How to Use It
Start by lightly misting your hair with hairspray and making sure it’s combed through and tangle-free. Choose a one-inch section of hair and position the ends at the open mouth of the curl chamber. When you close the chamber, the machine will automatically draw your hair inside, and if you choose a timer setting, it will beep to let you know when the curl is ready.

I was so thrilled to see this pop up today! Head over here to get a Rusk Curl Freak machine for just $49.99 shipped, usually $119.99!
Benefits
This machine is designed to create smooth, uniform curls without the strain and fuss of twisting a traditional curling iron.
How It Works
Hair is drawn into a ceramic curl chamber, where it’s coiled and heated up until each curl is set. Users can choose to release the hair on their own or opt for a pre-set timer that beeps when it’s time to set hair free after creating a loose wave, soft curl, or more-defined curl.
How to Use It
Start by lightly misting your hair with hairspray and making sure it’s combed through and tangle-free. Choose a one-inch section of hair and position the ends at the open mouth of the curl chamber. When you close the chamber, the machine will automatically draw your hair inside, and if you choose a timer setting, it will beep to let you know when the curl is ready.

posts.title: As Seen on Your Life A to Z...Money Saving MYTHS!
posts.excerpt: Thanks so much for tuning into my 3TV segment about money saving myths. If you haven’t already, I hope you’ll join the totally FREE Alicia’s Deals e-mail list…
posts.text:
Thanks so much for tuning into my 3TV segment about money saving myths. If you haven’t already, I hope you’ll join the totally FREE Alicia’s Deals e-mail list (unsubscribe at anytime). Please tell a friend about my site too so we can all “live life better for less” together. You can also find out first about the latest and greatest bargains when you “like” Alicia’s Deals on Facebook and follow me on Twitter.
MYTH: It's always cheaper to pay with cash.
Most people say that you'll always spend less with cash and I say that's just not true for everyone. If you do pay with cash, always ask if there's a cash discount. My nail salon gives 10% off for paying with cash.
If there's no discount, it's always better to use a high rewards credit card. There are so many out there, check out the benefits and figure out what's best for you. My card gives me 2.05% back to go toward travel, I like to say I pay 97.95% for everything. So if I put $25,000 a year on a credit card, that's over $500 back that I wouldn't have if I used cash. $25000 a year seems like a lot to put on a credit card, but if you use it at the grocery store, use it to pay your internet bill, use it on any bills that don't charge fees, you'll really see the bonuses add up. Just make sure you pay the bill in full each and every month. We should NEVER pay even one cent in credit card interest.
I like paying with credit cards better than debit cards because you get the added benefits and you get better protection in most cases than you do with a debit card. If someone steals your information with a credit card they won't have the ability to empty your bank account like they do with a debit card. Just make sure you're not spending money you wouldn't have spent with cash. Fiscal responsibility is key.
MYTH: It's usually more expensive to buy online than to shop in store.
Get in the habit of using FREE money saving programs. If you shop online a lot, make sure you're signed up for programs like Ebates and Top Cash Back. They give you a percentage back of whatever you buy. Search for promo codes wherever you're shopping, online it's really easy to combine promo codes to save the most money possible. At Kohl's you can combine up to four codes on the same item! If you use Ebates, you'll save even more on top of that.
MYTH: Costco is always a good deal
Costco does have some great prices, but they have some really high prices on items too. You can often find the same items for a lot less when they're on sale at the grocery stores, do your research. If you won't go through the items before they expire, it's definitely not a good deal to shop there. The one item I love at Costco is the $4.99 rotisserie chicken. It's consistently good and huge.
MYTH: If an Item You Already Bought Goes on Sale, Too Bad
Most stores will credit you the difference within a certain period of time, it's always worth a phone call or e-mail. You'll be amazed what stores will do to keep you from taking something back.

"The menu includes slow-smoked pork spareribs; a country-fried steak platter with housemade cream gravy, coleslaw, and mashed potatoes; and a creamed spinach and artichoke heart enchilada platter with southwestern sauce, tortilla chips, and salsa.
The four Dillon's locations couldn't be more different. The first location, which opened in 1999, was once described as "a cute, converted old house that looks like grandma's parlor" by the Phoenix New Times. There, guests devour Kansas City–style barbecue slathered in housemade sauces and listen to live music on Fridays and Saturdays. The combination of good food and relaxed ambiance proved to be so successful that Dillon's opened a second location in Glendale in 2005. This one plays host to golfers and sports enthusiasts, entertaining them with 30 HD-TVs, as well as with live bands on the weekends.
In 2011, Dillon's opened perhaps its most impressive location at the Wild Life World Zoo. Here, guests can dine beside a 60,000 gallon shark tank in the dining room and vibrant pink flamingoes on the patio and the year 2016 saw Dillon's expanding to Dillon's Bayou. In addition to its unique settings and food, Dillon's is known for its hospitality and sense of fun, including setting up live webcams of its Pleasant Harbor Marina and zoo locations. Check them out here."

For starters, there's the backdrop. Located not 5 miles from downtown Scottsdale, Sanctuary Spa is spread across 53 acres of pristine desert landscape. Then there are its multitudinous amenities, including 12 indoor and outdoor treatment rooms, a 25-meter lap pool, and a zen meditation garden and reflecting pond.
What truly makes the spa a sanctuary, however, is its selection of indulgent services. Read on to learn more about a few.
Five Star firming facial: This indulgent facial works to combat signs of aging. Using Astara Skin Care formulas, which are packed with antioxidants and nutrients, the aesthetician helps moisturize and firm skin, while protecting it from environmental damage.

Luk pra kope: Meaning "to massage with medicinal herbs," this Asian-inspired treatment starts with a fragrant kaffir-lime foot exfoliation. The therapist will then apply organic herbs along the body's meridians, concluding the service with a Thai massage that's augmented by a heated herbal compress.
Watsu: During this deeply relaxing 60-minute aquatic-therapy session, the client floats in warm water as a massage therapist gently cradles, rocks, and stretches the body. Because it takes place in the water, clients are able to increase their range of motion with less pain.

You could head over here and get a family four pack of tickets to the Arizona Science Center along with four tickets to their featured exhibition "Alien Worlds and Androids" for $41.25 with code FLY25, a $96 value. If you think you'll go to the Science Center more than once this year you can get a full one year membership for four along with two tickets to "Alien Worlds and Androids" for $59.25 with code FLY25, a $157 value.
"Alien Worlds and Androids, takes on the question that has fascinated man for centuries: “Are we alone?” Through the use of robots, telescopes, space probes and high-tech laboratories, scientists have been studying the possibility of life existing beyond Earth and what forms it may take depending on the environment. Opening Saturday, September 17, Alien Worlds and Androids brings guests face-to-face with worlds far beyond their own, and introduces the technology that takes them there.
Produced by Global Experience Specialists (GES), Alien Worlds and Androids , a 5,000 square foot exhibition, has nine areas highlighting their studies and findings: Are We Alone, Looking for Life in Space, Alien Life on Earth, Artificial Intelligence and Robots, Robot Space Explorers, Explore the Solar System, The Robotization of Planet Earth, I-Cyborg, and The Human Microbiome.
Sci-fi fans will appreciate how science fiction has inspired and influenced science, robotics and technologies. Life-size replicas of Iron Man, C-3PO and R2D2 from Star Wars movies, and a replica T-800 bust from The Terminator franchise, produce great learning and “selfie” photo opportunities. Guests are encouraged to construct an alien, touch a meteorite, work with a robotic arm, and sit in a POD to experience the incredible journey CURIOSTY endured to land on Mars."
Enjoy!

Petting zoo

About MacDonald's Ranch
There's something timeless about MacDonald's Ranch. Maybe it's that visitors can take a guided horseback ride through the desert, pose for an old-time photo, or ride a stagecoach—which in certain cases, might be held up by actors dressed as outlaws. But whatever the reason guests dock their zeppelin at MacDonald's Ranch, the staff hopes to treat them to a fun ranch experience. They surround them with music, cowboy shows, and seasonal attractions such as the annual pumpkin festival.
MacDonald's Ranch covers 1,300 acres of the scenic Sonoran Desert. Whether on horseback, train, or a hayride, guests can explore the area and view its desert flora, hawks, petrified spurs, and coyotes."

About The Crypt Haunted Attractions
No one knows where Dr. Vantas lost his way. Once an esteemed doctor at the vanguard of electroshock therapy for the mentally insane, the physician let his psychiatric hospital become a madhouse, prompting rumors of Vantas using inhumane experiments on patients. Those who enter his territory risk falling prey to its deranged denizens and the quack’s extremely cold stethoscope. This is the spine-tingling, horror-film narrative that plays out to visitors as they creep through The Asylum, a haunted site modeled after an 1870s-style mental institution and one third of of The Crypt Haunted Attractions’ three-piece tribute to fear.

Tiptoeing through the chamber's darkened corridors, voyagers must stay poised as they strafe around staggering corpses groaning about their hunger for brains or the lack of legroom in their casket. posts.title: Get Four $5 Groupons to Spend at Piccolo's Family Italian Ices for $11.40...One Of Our FAVORITE Places!
posts.excerpt: If you live in Scottsdale or will be visiting the area soon, you won't want to miss this! Head over here to get four $5 Groupons to spend at Piccolo's Family…
posts.text:
If you live in Scottsdale or will be visiting the area soon, you won't want to miss this! Head over here to get four $5 Groupons to spend at Piccolo's Family Italian Ice for $11.40 with code SUMMER20. This is one of our family's favorite places, their Italian Ice is out of this world and their Brooklyn style pizzas, fresh ciabatta sandwiches, and Hebrew National hot dogs on pretzel rolls are amazing too. Their prices are really reasonable to begin with, this deal is fantastic.
Don't take my word for it, check out this review in the Arizona Republic.
One of the best parts of this place is the people. It's family run and operated and it's always a treat to stop in and say hello. They have China Mist iced tea (they'll put in the most delicious fruit if you'd like to make it incredible) and tons of other menu items you'll enjoy. Our whole family loves the place and we stop in as often as we can.
"When the family behind Piccolo Family Italian Ice moved to Scottsdale, they were disappointed they couldn't find a place with East Coast–style pizza and sweet italian ices. They spent years dreaming about their old favorite noshes, before eventually deciding just to open up their own "Friday night slice and ice" joint.
Piccolo Family Italian Ice now serves up New York–style pizza (available whole or by the slice) made with imported crust from Brooklyn and italian ices in such flavors as lemon, Swedish fish, and rainbow. It also treats visitors to other East Coast favorites, from Hebrew National hot dogs to old-fashioned penny candy."
Check out their website and facebook page, and please say hello to Robin and the rest of the family for me if you stop in! So nice to support small business in our community!
Address
10135 E Via Linda, #C112
Scottsdale, AZ 85258
Phone
(480) 568-0988

Monday - Thursday: 11:30 a.m. - 8:00 p.m.
Friday - Saturday: 11:30 p.m. - 9:00 p.m.

The farm announced on facebook that this is the only opportunity to buy discounted tickets (I just checked Groupon and it says there are less than 10 hours left to save)!
“Admission includes access to:
7-acre corn maze
Giant jump pad
Extreme air pillow
Giant tube slide
Mini hay maze
Hop-along ponies
Spiderweb climb
Duck races
One barrel train ride
One tractor train ride
Petting zoo
The Vertuccio family shares 40 acres of Mesa countryside with families celebrating the autumn season. The 7-acre maize maze challenges visitors of all ages to race toward the finish line without stopping to hug lonely scarecrows, and the pumpkin patch displays a selection of nascent jack-o’-lanterns. Guests can swing by the petting zoo or hop aboard a pony ride for a chance to scratch behind fuzzy ears, and a roster of other rides and attractions lets tots check bounce houses and train rides off their crayon-scrawled bucket list. Free parking and a full concessions stand allow families to spend an entire afternoon at the farm, conjuring up a slew of smiles in the crisp fall air.”
The deal is good any day October 3rd-November 6th.
Enjoy!

Children's Museum of Phoenix
Although classrooms can be vibrant centers for learning, they’re usually stocked with pencils and notebooks instead of a forest of suspended green noodles or a flying bathtub with wings. At the Children's Museum of Phoenix, both of these engage young minds alongside other hands-on exhibits that have earned the museum a glut of awards, including a place among Parents magazine’s 10 Best Children’s Museums in 2011. The museum fosters creativity and skill development in children from birth to age 10 with open-ended play activities that range from bouncing orbs in the Grand Ballroom to building forts with a wealth of safe construction materials, instead of mom’s favorite sheets and a nail gun.
Perhaps the most eye-catching feature of the museum can be found in the atrium, where the Schuff-Perini Climber soars high into the air. Created from standard building materials, found objects, and out-of-context items such as its flying bathtub, the structure entices youths and inspires their imaginations. Another impressive contraption makes up the Whoosh! exhibit, where children feed scarves into a jumble of tubes that suck the fabrics up to heights of 20 feet before spitting them out to float gently down and be caught in waiting fingers. At each of these exhibits, a baby zone keeps the tiniest museum-goers safe, and they can find a space especially for them in the Place for Threes & Younger."

posts.title: Happy First Friday! FREE Admission to Lots of Fun Museums!
posts.excerpt: Hooray! Today (5/6) is First Friday! If you don’t have plans, you may want to head to Downtown Phoenix to enjoy some FREE museums! Anyone that says Phoenix has…
posts.text:
Hooray! Today (5/6) is First Friday! If you don’t have plans, you may want to head to Downtown Phoenix to enjoy some FREE museums! Anyone that says Phoenix has no culture has obviously never been to First Friday!
Head to the Children’s Museum of Phoenix where everyone will get in free from 5-9 PM. Tickets are usually $11 each, so this is quite an opportunity to play for less!
Still have energy? Go to the Phoenix Art Museum for their First Friday event.Everyone will get in for free from 6-10 PM (tickets are usually $15 for adults, $6 for kids).
They have tons of fun planned tonight:
"La Dolce Vita Garden Party, Dorrance Sculpture Garden
FREE, 6-10pm, Cash Bar
In celebration of our current fashion exhibition The White Shirt According to Me: Gianfranco Ferré, we’re throwing a fabulous Italian themed garden party for everyone to enjoy.
Activities:
- Outdoor film screening of Italian Classic La Dolce Vita outside in the Dorrance Sculpture garden at 7pm.
- Glamorous vintage fashions on view from Rare Scarf, Vintage by Misty and Fashion by Robert Black.
- Fashion presentation by student designers from the Art Institute of Phoenix.
- Italian cocktails, popcorn and espresso.
- Arts and crafts inspired by Italian fashion.
- FREE photo booth.
- Guided exhibition tours.
Free exhibition admission, one night only.
phxart.org / @phxart"
If it’s date night, you might want to think about checking out the Arizona Science Center. Adults 18 and over will get in for free (general admission). Head over here for more information.
Visit the Heard Museum for their First Friday Native + You program.Everyone will get into the museum FOR FREE from 6-10 (tickets are usually $18 for adults, $7.50 for kids).
Enjoy and have fun!

If you don't have a thermometer you love, head over here to pick up a Kinsa Smart Thermometer for $14.99 shipped (usually $20-$30). We have one and it has some really neat features. I love that the kids get to play games while their temperature is taken and that the app allows you to track temperatures and symptoms over time...super helpful when you go to the doctor. Each child (and adult) can have their own profile. This has won tons of awards and is a great value (I'm not sure when they'll raise the price back up).
"By using your smartphone, Kinsa takes advantage of 25,000X the processing power of a regular digital thermometer. Tapping into the smartphone’s power, processing and display also means there are virtually no electronics inside – and no batteries are required – so the thermometer is extremely lightweight and durable for carrying with you, and is always ready for use.
Kinsa’s team of top engineers have implemented the latest technology in machine learning and data science to ensure you are always getting the most accurate and efficient reading possible—and one that continues to improve with every app update.
Kinsa also detects if your thermometer isn’t in an ideal position, helping you settle back in place for a more accurate reading.
Kinsa is thin and flexible, making it not only more comfortable, but also the most unbreakable thermometer on the market for all ages. Kids love Kinsa’s bubble popping game, bright colors, and simple, visual symptom options so much that they don’t only stay put for readings, they ask for Kinsa again and again.
10 second average read time
Exceeds both ASTM and ISO standards for professional accuracy
For use by infants, children and adults
For use orally, under the arm or rectally
Clean with soap & water or alcohol, or use with a standard disposable probe cover

posts.text:
Teacher Appreciation Day is May 3rd this year (TOMORROW) and I’m trying to put together all of the deals I can find to celebrate the WONDERFUL teachers our kids learn from! Thank you so much for all you do!
Chipotle: “In honor of Teacher Appreciation Day, we’re giving all educators a BOGO. Teachers, faculty and staff: bring in your school ID to any Chipotle in the U.S. on Tuesday, May 3rd, 2016 from 3pm–close to receive a BUY-ONE/GET-ONE BURRITOS, BOWLS, SALADS, or ORDER OF TACOS. “
Organ Stop Pizza: Teachers can “come in to Organ Stop Pizza in Mesa between May 2 and May 6th, 2016 during regular business hours, (5 p.m. – 9 p.m.), and get a gift card for a free pizza*. Any size pizza, no limit on toppings. Value up to $20.
Must be an employed K-12 teacher and show valid school ID. (Working at a school does not qualify).
*Free Pizzas are for dine-in only.
*Free pizza coupon may be redeemed immediately or on a future visit.
*Coupons expire 8/31/16″

Whether guests are coming for a drink after the bell rings or thinking about pairing their brew during dinner plans, WOB wants to reward America’s educators by inviting them to enjoy a cold one at locations across the country by presenting a valid teacher ID. posts.title: Chipotle Cultivate Festival is This Saturday! Free Festival With Music, Chef Demonstrations, and More! Earn a Free Burrito!
posts.excerpt: The Chipotle Cultivate festival is coming to town this Saturday, April 30th at Westworld. Admission is free as are all of the musical acts and activities!…
posts.text:
The Chipotle Cultivate festival is coming to town this Saturday, April 30th at Westworld. Admission is free as are all of the musical acts and activities! Parking is $5 and you can earn a free burrito when you participate in interactive food experiences with their passport!
Check out the info about the freebie: "Visit the five experiences around the festival, learn from what they have to offer, and get your program stamped. Once you’ve completed at least three, bring your program to the Info Tent and you’ll receive a coupon for a FREE burrito, bowl, salad or order of tacos and IZZE at any Chipotle."
Check out a little bit more information about the event:
"Cultivate Phoenix encourages attendees to think and talk about food and food issues, as well as how to create a more sustainable future. While many festival-goers come for the entertainment, the free festival also offers interactive experiences for all ages to learn something new about how food is raised and prepared.
At the festival, renowned chefs from Phoenix and around the country will offer cooking demonstrations and seminars. Additionally, six national musical acts will perform throughout the day, including Young the Giant, Echosmith, Lukas Graham, Betty Who, Holychild and Jared & The Mill.
The high-profile chefs involved with Cultivate Phoenix are working to make positive changes in the nation’s food supply. Participating in Cultivate Phoenix allows these chefs to bring awareness to the public while demonstrating the impact food has on society and the importance of food that is raised right. The lineup of featured chefs includes Aaron Sanchez (Chef/Partner at Johnny Sanchez in New Orleans and Baltimore, host of Cooking Channel’s Taco Trip, and judge on Food Network’s “Chopped”); Amanda Freitag (co-host of Food Network’s “American Diner Revival,” judge on “Chopped,” and author of “The Chef Next Door”); Chris Bianco (Pizzeria Bianco in Phoenix and Tucson, and Pane Bianco in Phoenix); Stephen Jones (the larder + the delta); and Charleen Badman (FnB Restaurant) with Pavle Milic (FnB Restaurant, Los Milics Wine).
Chipotle will be serving up burritos, tacos and menu items from ShopHouse Southeast Asian Kitchen, Chipotle’s Asian concept. Each dish will be made using fresh, responsibly grown ingredients.
The festival will have an Artisans’ Hall featuring local artisanal desserts and sweet treats for purchase. Wine, beer and hard cider from local Phoenix breweries and wineries will be available for those 21 and older to purchase at the Tasting Hall. Chipotle has also partnered with three nationally acclaimed breweries, including Phoenix-based Arizona Wilderness to create a “Cultivate Mexican Lager” brewed exclusively for the three 2016 Cultivate festivals in Phoenix, Kansas City and Miami.
Cultivate Phoenix includes interactive experiences focused on sustainable food, and a Kids’ Zone with activities and snacks for the entire family. The experiences will allow attendees to explore the importance of animal welfare; issues surrounding genetically modified foods, or GMOs; the secret to making Chipotle’s famous guacamole; the reality of processed foods; and best practices for preparing food safely.
For more information, please visit: Chipotle.com/Cultivate"
Thanks Libby!
Enjoy!

"Spread across 20 acres, dozens of rides, slides, and water attractions send visitors splashing through scorching summer days. At the Waikiki Beach wave pool, 2.5 million gallons of water swell and swirl to create refreshing waves every three minutes. Captain Cook’s Landing cools down toddlers, and winding slides tout the names of natural phenomena such as Cyclone, Tsunami, and Tom Hanks. The water park is accompanied by free parking. Rafts, boogie boards, and surfboards are available to rent.
Big Surf Waterpark
In 1966, Big Surf Waterpark founder Phil Dexter built his first model of a wave machine in his backyard, a place he affectionally named Tahiti Phil's. With some help, and several models later—including one assembled inside an abandoned billiards hall—he perfected the contraption, making it the centerpiece of his newly opened waterpark in 1969. Dexter's invention instantly snagged press from Time, Sports Illustrated, and Life, and today, it remains Big Surf Waterpark's 2.5-million-gallon keynote attraction. One of Big Surf Waterpark's newest attractions is the Mauna Kea Zip Line, which starts high in the air before zipping over the wave pool. Over the years, despite Arizona's lack of rain or gigantic sprinkler, the park has managed to grow around the wave pool, and its current 20-acre campus features dozens of slides, rides, and areas for all ages. Big Surf's real estate has also played host to entertainment events, including concerts from Pink Floyd, Elton John, and the Beach Boys."

posts.title: Admission for Two to the Biosphere 2 for $21 (Usually $40)! We Just Went and Learned a Ton!
posts.excerpt: Promo code BIG25 (25% off your Groupon purchase for select accounts) is really coming in handy today to get your late spring/early summer adventures PLANNED!…
posts.text:
Promo code BIG25 (25% off your Groupon purchase for select accounts) is really coming in handy today to get your late spring/early summer adventures PLANNED! If your account wasn't selected please let me know if you have a code I can add!
Head over here to get admission for two to the Biosphere 2 for $21 (usually $40) with code BIG25. We just went last weekend and learned a ton. It was so interesting to see the rainforest next to the ocean next to the desert. The stories of the people who lived there were really interesting too...they lost a ton of weight and didn't have enough oxygen for the first 2 year experiment. I can imagine the cabin fever was incredibly intense. Even though no one lives there any more, they are still constantly doing experiments and learning more about Biosphere 1 (our world).
"In 1984, Space Biospheres Ventures purchased a few unassuming acres north of Tucson in the shadow the Santa Catalina Mountains. There, the company expanded its sci-fi-sounding activities—the development of space-colonization technology—and built what would evolve into Biosphere 2, recently seen on The Today Show.
Designed to re-create Earth's ecosystems, the gigantic glass enclosure (some 7.2 million cubic feet and 91 feet tall in some parts) is famous for housing biospherians in the 1990s. The researchers lived completely sealed inside for extended periods, giving scientists groundbreaking data on human survivability and interaction with particular bionetworks.
The University of Arizona had the 40-acre Biosphere 2 campus donated in 2011, maintaining it as a hub of serious research while expanding its mission to encompass interactive educational outreach. Each year, thousands pass through the on-site labs and classrooms as well as stroll the Biosphere 2 interior to view films, experience multimedia exhibits, or embark on guided tours. Tours venture into the actual ecosystems, allowing earthlings to note biodiversity, smell fresh precipitation in the rain forest, and savor the softness of savannah grassland underfoot until the resident grumpy old man yells at you to get the heck off his lawn. Before their dramatic conclusion at a million-gallon ocean tank, tours delve into the basement to explore the technosphere, where visitors can witness the deep inhales and exhales of the sphere’s respiratory system."
Enjoy!

posts.title: My Favorite Deals at the Grocery Stores This Week!
posts.excerpt: It’s time once again for my favorite deals at the grocery stores!
posts.text:

Download the Ibotta app here if you haven’t already. You can get money back from your purchases at grocery stores including Sprouts, Fry’s, Safeway, Whole Foods, WinCo Foods, Albertsons and more (think $.50 back from any Post cereal, $.75 back from Kashi cereal, $1 back from Red Baron pizza, $1.50 back from Canada Dry sparkling seltzer water, $.25 back from milk, $.25 back from bananas, $.50 back from Reynolds baking pans, $.75 back from Kleenex, $5 back from Mucinex night time, $3 back from Tecate beer, $2 back from Heineken, $5 back from Skinny Girl wine, and more). posts.title: Feeling Bored This Spring Break? Don't Forget to Get Your Pogo Passes!
posts.excerpt: Spring Break is THIS WEEK for many AZ kiddos! If you’re staying in town and looking for fun stuff to do, get a Pogo Pass. Head over here and use code ALICIA…
posts.text:
Spring Break is THIS WEEK for many AZ kiddos! If you’re staying in town and looking for fun stuff to do, get a Pogo Pass. Head over here and use code ALICIA and get 60% off (you’ll pay $39.98 instead of $99.99). This is truly one of the best deals in family entertainment out there. You’ll enjoy a FULL YEAR of admissions to places all over town (each place has their own details about how many times you get in with the pass).
The Play Factory is now included with the pass in Desert Ridge. My daughter Kaitlyn had her birthday party here one year and had a great time. Here’s more information about the place:
“Each Pogo Pass holder receives Three (3) “All Day Admission Passes” to Play Factory, during ALL Regular Open Play Hours. “
Locally owned and family operated, The Play Factory is where everyone can climb, jump, bounce, slide, and weave their way through hours of fun exercise and entertainment! We crank out fun, with an all-ages indoor playground, a 20-foot rock wall, a large inflatable slide, and a separate safety zone and bounce house for toddlers 4 and under, even parents can get in on the excitement. Arcade games, an X Box Play, as well as fresh cotton candy and over 9 flavors of shaved-ice sweeten the deal! “
The pass includes so much more too! Passes are good during regular business hours (unless otherwise noted) and venues are subject to change.
Castles and Coasters: Each Pogo Pass holder recieves One (1) visit to Castles~n~Coasters for a *Silver Pass. *Silver pass is good for Unlimited rides and 1 round of miniature golf.
The Phoenix Zoo: Each Pogo Pass holder receives general admission to the Phoenix Zoo two (2) times.
Sunsplash: Each pass holder can attend Golfland Sunsplash one (1) time. Your pass is good for one (1) SunSplash General admission ticket starting May 16th, 2015 when full park opens for the season.
Arizona Diamondbacks: *One (1) ticket per game for Two (2) Arizona Diamondbacks home games. Available home games are posted under available hours.
Phoenix Rock Gym: Pogo Pass holders can attend Phoenix Rock Gym two (2) times.
Skateland: Each pass holder can attend Skateland two (2) times per month. Skateland has three (3) different locations available to pass holders.
Makutus Island: Each Pogo Pass holder receives general admission to Makutu’s Island two (2) times. Available during regular business hours Monday-Friday. Excludes these major holidays: Memorial Day, Independance Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day and Veterans Day.
Fat Cats: *Each Pogo Pass member recieves 1 (one) game of bowling per week, and 1 (One) Glow Golf visit per month. Shoe rental not included. Outside food and drink prohibited. Available Monday-Thursday 11:00am-10:00pm, Fridays 11:00am-5pm. (Excludes Friday’s after 5pm, Saturdays, Sundays and ALL Holidays)
Pump it Up: Each Pogo Pass holder receives general admission to Pump It Up two (2) times. (Tempe and Peoria locations). Available Monday – Friday, excludes all major holidays and special events.
IDEA Museum: Each pass holder can attend i.d.e.a Museum two (2) times during normal business hours.
Arizona Rattlers: *One (1) ticket per game for Three (3) Arizona Rattlers home games. Available home games are posted under available hours.
ASU Athletics: Pogo Pass is a accepted for general admission tickets to ALL of the following ASU athletic home games: Women’s Basketball, Soccer, Wrestling, Volleyball, Gymnastics, Track and Field
Phoenix Mercury: *One (1) ticket per game, for Three (3) Phoenix Mercury home games. Available home games are posted under available hours.
Tempe Paintball: *Each Pogo Pass member can attend Tempe Paintball one (1) time per month. Each paintball visit includes gun rental, air, and 100 paintballs. Each Airsoft visit includes admission, equipment rental package and 200 BB’s. Available regular business hours excluding Saturdays. Tempe Paintball strongly suggest that you make an online reservation to ensure availability of equipment. Please click on the link below to book your visit http://bit.ly/1TGGMLW.
Enchanted Island: Your Pogo Pass is good for a Day Pass four (4) times at Enchanted Island Park. Limited capacity, first come first serve. Some rides may require additional charge. Good Fridays and Sundays, excluding special events.
Stratum Laser Tag: Pogo Pass holders can attend Stratum Laser Tag two (2) separate times, Pogo Passes may be used on Mondays and Wednesdays 4:30-close. Pogo Passes may not be used during school holiday breaks or Stratum’s designated holiday hours.
You could do so much this spring break!
Enjoy!

posts.text:
Head over here to enjoy 15% off the deal of your choice at Living Social with code TREAT15.
You could enjoy two tickets to the Scottsdale Culinary Festival coming April 16th and 17th for $10.19 with code TREAT15, usually $20. You can choose the date of your choice, but I'm guessing Saturday will sell out pretty quickly!
If you've never been before it's tons of fun.
"Highlights: 40 Local Restaurants, 30 Craft Breweries, 20 Bands, Teen Cooking Challenge, Chef Demos, Family Zone, Wine Garden, Vodka Lounge, and More!
Arizona's tastiest fundraiser, the Scottsdale Culinary Festival is back at the Scottsdale Civic Center Mall for two delicious days (April 16 and 17) of culinary creations from 40 local restaurants. With general admission, you'll get access to the culinary experience tent, chef demos, wine seminars, a teen cooking challenge, live entertainment and expanded family zone.
The 25-acre Scottsdale Culinary Festival grounds feature eleven themed zones jam-packed with interactive experiences that'll help you taste, sip, and celebrate Arizona's awesome food culture. Bring extra cash to purchase food and beverages, which are sold separately."
Enjoy!

“By using your smartphone, Kinsa takes advantage of 25,000X the processing power of a regular digital thermometer. 10 second average read time
Exceeds both ASTM and ISO standards for professional accuracy
For use by infants, children and adults
For use orally, under the arm or rectally
Clean with soap & water or alcohol, or use with a standard disposable probe cover
Optional extension cord allows you and your child to watch and interact with the screen while in use”

“The Smart Ear uses a Bluetooth LE connection, sometimes called Bluetooth 4.0, and will be compatible with a wide variety of Apple and Android phones. To successfully sync readings between the thermometer and app, Kinsa requires iOS 8.1 or above on compatible Apple phones and Android KitKat (v 4.4) or above on compatible Android phones. “
The reviews are phenomenal, it has won many awards, and families love it. No worrying about batteries or long temperature times! I wish I had this for the last month!

"In 1984, Space Biospheres Ventures purchased a few unassuming acres north of Tucson in the shadow the Santa Catalina Mountains. There, the company expanded its sci-fi-sounding activities—the development of space-colonization technology—and built what would evolve into Biosphere 2, recently seen on The Today Show.
Designed to re-create Earth's ecosystems, the gigantic glass enclosure (some 7.2 million cubic feet and 91 feet tall in some parts) is famous for housing biospherians in the 1990s. The researchers lived completely sealed inside for extended periods, giving scientists groundbreaking data on human survivability and interaction with particular bionetworks.
The University of Arizona had the 40-acre Biosphere 2 campus donated in 2011, maintaining it as a hub of serious research while expanding its mission to encompass interactive educational outreach. Each year, thousands pass through the on-site labs and classrooms as well as stroll the Biosphere 2 interior to view films, experience multimedia exhibits, or embark on guided tours. Tours venture into the actual ecosystems, allowing earthlings to note biodiversity, smell fresh precipitation in the rain forest, and savor the softness of savannah grassland underfoot until the resident grumpy old man yells at you to get the heck off his lawn. Before their dramatic conclusion at a million-gallon ocean tank, tours delve into the basement to explore the technosphere, where visitors can witness the deep inhales and exhales of the sphere’s respiratory system."
I've always wanted to go!
Enjoy!

Feel like getting married on Valentine's Day? You could have a free ceremony on Sunday, February 14th at the Maricopa County Justice Center. Check out the details :
"Saturday and Sunday Hours, Free Wedding Ceremonies for Valentine’s Day
Clerk of the Superior Court Michael Jeanes will open the Customer Service Center from 9:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m. on Saturday, February 13, 2016 and from 10:30 a.m. until 2:30 p.m. on Sunday, February 14, 2016 at 601 W. Jackson St. in downtown Phoenix to issue marriage licenses and process passport applications.
To compliment this event, the Maricopa County Justice Courts will offer free wedding ceremonies on Valentine’s Day, February 14, 2016 inside the Downtown Justice Center located at 620 W. Jackson St., across the street from the Clerk’s offices. Free weddings are only available at this location on Valentine’s Day from 11:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. on a walk-in basis. Several Justices of the Peace will perform ceremonies and couples should bring at least two witnesses in addition to their marriage license. Family and friends may attend as well.
The marriage license fee is $76, payable by cash, debit card, money order, Visa, MasterCard or American Express only and the license must be used within one year of the date issued. There are additional fees for a certified copy of the recorded license. For information on other requirements, see the Clerk’s website at http://www.clerkofcourt.maricopa.gov/marlic.asp.
The Clerk’s Office processes applications for passport books and cards for children and adults. The U.S. Department of State and Clerk of Court fees are paid separately. The Clerk’s $25 fee applies to each application and is payable by cash, debit card, money order, Visa, MasterCard or American Express only. The entire experience takes about 2–3 hours to complete and consists of 10–17 obstacles on each of the five courses, which range from rope swings to wobbly bridges and ziplines. Before exploring the courses, visitors must pass a 30-minute safety training, where they learn how to put on their harnesses and navigate the courses. Flagstaff Extreme Adventure Course
A shorter and equally appropriate name for Flagstaff Extreme Adventure Course would be Endor. Spread throughout the ponderosa pines of Fort Tuthill County Park, the course’s rope swings, wobbly bridges, scrambling walls, and hanging nets resemble the Ewoks’ home planet in Star Wars: Episode VI. Ground patrols and course guides add another layer of reassurance, as do the courses themselves, color-coded to signal their difficulty level. I found a new site I love called Schoola. Head over here to get a FREE $20 credit toward adorable, slightly used kids clothes. Right now you can save $10 off your $30 baby purchase with code BABYLOVE10 plus get 30% off with your Kohls charge with code LOVE2SHOP plus get free shipping on any size purchase with your Kohls charge with code FREE4MVC. This would be a fun, MEMORABLE Valentine's date! Head over here to get tickets to Becoming Dr. Ruth at the Herberger for $35 (plus $5.50 service fee), usually $49-$53.
There are lots of February dates available.
"Let's talk about sex. Everyone knows Dr. Ruth Westheimer from her career as a pioneering and straight-talking radio and TV sex therapist. Very few, however, know the truly incredible journey that preceded it. Learn about America's most famous sexpert, whose amazing life story includes such unbelievable exploits as fleeing from the Nazis in the Kindertransport, joining the Israeli Haganah as a scout and sniper (yes, you read that right -- 4'7" Dr. Ruth was a skilled sniper) and struggling to succeed as a single mother while adjusting to life in America. Becoming Dr. Ruth was called "fascinating and heartbreaking" by The New York Times. Penned by Mark St. Germain, the play is filled with all the humor, honesty and life-affirming spirit of its titular hero, the diminutive woman with a huge personality who became synonymous with something she truly loved -- sex."
I had no idea she was a sniper!
Click on "send karma codes" to send $10 off codes to your friends!
Enjoy!

posts.title: Ultimate Good Deal: FREE MBA at ASU (a $54,000 Value for In-State Students)!
posts.excerpt: What a great deal for all of us in AZ who have been thinking about getting an MBA. The WP Carey School will be offering 120 FULL RIDES to full time MBA…
posts.text:
What a great deal for all of us in AZ who have been thinking about getting an MBA. The WP Carey School will be offering 120 FULL RIDES to full time MBA students (a $54000 value for in state students).
Check out the info from AZCentral:
"Maybe an MBA could be in your future after all.
Arizona State University is hoping to lure more people who wouldn't normally be thinking about a graduate business degree, or couldn't afford it, with a broad scholarship offer that could waive tuition and fees for next year's full crop of students.
The W. P. Carey School of Business plans to offer scholarships to the entire class in the full-time master's of business administration program starting with the 2016-2017 academic year, said Amy Hillman, the school's dean. The school is anticipating about 120 students next year, but the total could be higher.
Full-time tuition currently runs about $54,000 for the two-year program for Arizona residents, $87,000 for non-resident U.S. citizens and $90,000 for students from foreign countries. Applications are now being accepted for the 2016-2017 academic year.
A focus of the blanket scholarship offer is to encourage prospective entrepreneurs and people willing to work in the non-profit sector, within a broader giving-back-to-society theme. Funding for the program will be provided by the original endowment from the late William Polk Carey, a New York financier.
In the case of entrepreneurs, saving on tuition and fees can help free up money that could be used to launch a business, Hillman said. As for non-profits, many of these entities typically don't pay top wages and often have trouble attracting managerial talent, she said.
"These are examples of the types of people who might not see an MBA as possible," Hillman said, while adding that school officials wouldn't force applicants to go down particular career paths.
Amy Hillman is the dean of the W. P. Carey School of Business at Arizona State University.
Hillman said she hopes more women will apply for the scholarship offer. Women are underrepresented in the full-time MBA program, with 30 percent of the total, yet they make up a large number of non-profit employees and workers generally. The program also could help advance the Arizona economy, especially if it encourages entrepreneurs to start companies here, she said.
Hillman said the scholarship offer will be paired with a pay-it-forward theme, under which students will be asked later to serve as mentors and provide job-search help for those who follow in their footsteps. Many other universities offer MBA scholarships, but Hillman said she thought the blanket ASU offer, with its focus on giving back to society, was unusual.
ASU has 86 students in the first year of its full-time MBA program, for which the average age is 28. In the current class, 25 percent of the students come from other nations.
Hillman said prospective students should have the intellect and discipline to pursue the program, which she described as rigorous.
The scholarship offer won't help current full-time MBA students or those in the online or part-time programs. ASU has a total of 779 MBA students, including 336 in the online program, 196 in the part-time evening program, 144 in the two-year full-time program, 66 in the executive program, 32 in the weekend part-time program and 5 in the technology MBA program."
Enjoy!

posts.title: Happy First Friday! Free Admission to Lots of Fun Places Around Town!
posts.excerpt: Hooray! Today (10/2) is First Friday! If you don’t have plans, you may want to head to Downtown Phoenix to enjoy some FREE museums! Anyone that says Phoenix…
posts.text:
Hooray! Today (10/2) is First Friday! If you don’t have plans, you may want to head to Downtown Phoenix to enjoy some FREE museums! Anyone that says Phoenix has no culture has obviously never been to First Friday!
Head to the Children’s Museum of Phoenix where everyone will get in free from 5-9 PM. Tickets are usually $11 each, so this is quite an opportunity to play for less!
Still have energy? Go to the Phoenix Art Museum for their First Friday event. Everyone will get in for free from 6-10 PM (tickets are usually $15 for adults, $6 for kids).
If it’s date night, you might want to think about checking out the Arizona Science Center. Adults 18 and over will get in for free (general admission). Head over here for more information and to check out the lecture series.
Visit the Heard Museum for their First Friday Native + You program.Everyone will get into the museum FOR FREE from 6-10 (tickets are usually $18 for adults, $7.50 for kids).
Enjoy and have fun!

posts.excerpt: Head over here to save up to $16 off tickets to the MacDonald Ranch pumpkin patch in North Scottsdale!
posts.text:
Head over here to save up to $16 off tickets to the MacDonald Ranch pumpkin patch in North Scottsdale!
A little bit more info:
"Choose from Six Options
$16 for fall-festival admission for two ($24 value)
$24 for fall-festival admission for three ($36 value)
$32 for fall-festival admission for four ( $48 value)
The fall attractions are open October 1–31 except on Tuesdays. Fall attractions include:
Horse- or mule-drawn hayride or train ride to the pumpkin patch
Petting zoo
Pony rides (extra $3 per rider)
Hay maze
Western-themed games such as panning for gold and ring toss
Peddle cars (up to 150lbs weight limit)
There's something timeless about MacDonald's Ranch. Maybe it's that visitors can take a guided horseback ride through the desert, pose for an old-time photo, or ride a stagecoach—which in certain cases, might be held up by actors dressed as outlaws. But whatever the reason guests dock their zeppelin at MacDonald's Ranch, the staff hopes to treat them to a fun ranch experience. They surround them with music, cowboy shows, and seasonal attractions such as the annual pumpkin festival.
MacDonald's Ranch covers 1,300 acres of the scenic Sonoran Desert. Whether on horseback, train, or a hayride, guests can explore the area and view its desert flora, hawks, petrified spurs, and coyotes."
I love that this is good any day they are open!
Enjoy!

posts.text:
If you're thinking about buying a new car this Labor Day weekend, start here with Edmunds and get quotes online from dealerships all over town (when you have people fighting over you it's always a good thing). You'll have a number before you even leave the house, no tense negotiations required.
It's a great time to save on the 2015 models as the 2016s are coming. Here are some deals that Edmunds says are especially good:
"2015 BMW 3 Series
For those looking to enter the luxury market, discounts on this entry vehicle may be an attractive offer. The 3 Series includes sedan and hatchback models, and scores four out of five in J.D. Power ratings for overall quality. However, the 3 Series scores three out of five, or “about average” for predicted reliability.
In some regions, the 3 Series is already being sold for more than $1,500 below its true market value, or the Edmunds.com-calculated standard price customers pay based on past sales, which starts at about $32,950 for the gas engine sedan. The site expects BMW dealers to advertise cash rebates, lease specials and low-interest financing for end-of-summer deals on the 2015 model.
2015 Chevrolet Volt
Chevy’s GM, +1.05% take on the plug-in hybrid is slated for a major redesign later this year, which means big discounts are on the horizon for the 2015 model. Low gas prices this year have stifled demand for the environmentally friendly vehicle, so prices will be especially reduced. Reed says hybrids continue to see a decline in demand due to standard engines becoming more fuel efficient.
“There are some really good non-hybrid options now that have come up over the last five or six years,” Reed says. “They’ve stolen some thunder from hybrids.”
Edmunds.com estimates that most current offers on the 2015 Volt are already $4,000 below its true market value. Though the model scored four out five for predicted reliability in the J.D. Power ratings, its overall quality score was just two out of five, suggesting it may not be the best bang for your buck. The MSRP on the Volt is $34,345.
2015 Honda Civic
This highly rated model may be seeing discounts up to $2,000 below its true market value, according to Edmunds.com. The Honda Civic HMC, +1.59% sedan has an A rating from the site, and scores five out of five for overall quality and predicted reliability in J.D. Power ratings. Despite the high marks, the Civic rates about average for overall performance and design.
Reed says the Civic is one of the more popular models he was surprised to see on the list of Labor Day discounts, making this deal especially “attractive.”
The 2015 Honda Civic Hybrid’s manufacturer’s suggested retail price starts at $24,735.
2015 Toyota Prius
Suffering from the same gas price-induced stagnation as the Chevrolet Volt, dealers are cutting Toyota PriusTM, +2.37% prices down as much as $3,000 below true market value to stimulate demand, says Edmunds.com. Toyota is also offering an additional 0% financing for 60 months to qualified buyers to sweeten the deal. The MSRP on the Prius is $24,200.
Reed attributes the deep discount to the upcoming redesign for the 2016 model. The Prius has not been redesigned since 2004, giving it a relatively outdated body design. If you aren’t picky about looks, however, the offers on the 2015 model are a great way to save money.
“For people that are concerned about saving money, these cars are perfect for them,” Reed says.
Though the Prius scores low for overall quality and overall performance and design, it holds a perfect score for predicted reliability in the J.D. Power ratings.
2015 Volkswagen Passat
While Volkswagen isn’t implementing a total redesign of the midsize sedan for 2016, Edmunds.com estimates that the planned mid-cycle refresh is pushing prices down by $1,000 below true market value, in addition to cash incentives and 0% financing.
MSRP for the Passat starts at $21,340, however it has relatively average ratings, scoring three out of five for overall quality and two out of five for predicted reliability in the J.D. Power ratings."
Thanks Market Watch!

posts.title: HOT! Up to 54% off Octane Raceway Races!
posts.excerpt: Head over here to save up to 5% off Octane Raceway races in Scottsdale! This is supposed to be so much fun! Keep in mind that junior drivers must be at least…
posts.text:
Head over here to save up to 5% off Octane Raceway races in Scottsdale! This is supposed to be so much fun! Keep in mind that junior drivers must be at least 54 inches tall.
Check out the details:
"Choose from Four Options
$20 for two races and helmet rental for one person, valid Monday–Thursday only ($42.85 value)
$39 for four races and helmet rental for up to two, valid Monday–Thursday only (up to $85.70 value)
$25 for two races and helmet rental for one person, valid any time ($42.85 value)
$49 for four races and helmet rental for up to two, valid any time (up to $85.70 value)
Octane Raceway
It's hard to say which is more distinctive: the karts zipping around Octane Raceway or the track itself. During each lap on the 1/3-mile course, drivers zoom through an indoor area, then weave around an outdoor section that's covered by a permanent steel canopy, making for a hybrid experience rarely found in American go-kart tracks not owned by bored supervillains.
An equally rare find in the U.S. is the raceway's fleet of 32 Sodi RTX karts, all imported from France, whose electric motors give off zero emissions while reaching speeds of up to 45 miles per hour. Drivers who can stay in control at these top speeds are in for success: the winner of each race is determined not by who finishes a given number of laps first, but by who puts up the fastest single lap time, a result that's posted both at the track and online for posterity.
Races take place in a 65,000-square-foot space that doubles as a gathering place for parties and corporate events for up to 500 attendees. In addition to racing, the raceway is also home to off-track activities that include shooting pool in the billiards room, arcade games, and melting burgers and pizza into rocket fuel at the Trackside Bar and Grill."

Just for “joining” the event online and stopping by you’ll get a free gift!
“Discover the newest American Girl store, coming soon to Scottsdale Quarter! You and your girl are invited to join in the fun during our grand-opening weekend. She’ll enjoy free crafts, exciting activities, and doll drawings, and receive a FREE gift—just for attending! Gift available while supplies last.
Please “join” this event to receive important line queue information during grand opening weekend. Ticket distribution for the grand opening is on-site and by joining this event, it does not guarantee you a place in line or entry to the store. Please visit the check-in desk upon arrival for ticket distribution.”
Here’s more information about how to get tickets:
“Scottsdale Quarter, Scottsdale AZ – Grand Opening
Ticket Entry Process:
To manage guests’ waiting times and observe fire-safety regulations, a ticket system will be used for the American Girl Scottsdale – Scottsdale Quarter Grand-Opening Weekend.
Each person (including children) who wishes to enter the store will receive a ticket with an assigned group number.
We recommend parking in the Scottsdale Quarter parking structures: South Garage, East entrance.
Directional signs will be visible.
American Girl guests must visit the Quad, where the fountain is located, as their first stop to obtain tickets for entrance into the store.
Ticket distribution for Saturday admittance begins at 7 a.m. on Saturday, August 22nd.
Saturday tickets are valid for Saturday only.
Ticket distribution for Sunday admittance begins at 8 a.m. on Sunday, August 23rd.
Sunday tickets are valid for Sunday only.
Overnight camping is not allowed on property.
When the store opens each day, groups will be announced in numerical order for admittance through the American Girl entrance adjacent to the main entrance on 73rd.
You can shop or dine in Scottsdale Quarter until your group number is called. If you have a Bistro reservation, you can come directly to the ticket-distribution table, as check-in is allowed up to two hours prior to your Bistro reservation time. The ticket-distribution table will be located outside the store.
Facebook message alerts will be available, providing updates on group numbers being admitted; details below.
Access the event page starting Saturday, August 22nd on your mobile device.
Once Facebook is open, search “American Girl” -
When on the page, scroll down until “Upcoming Events” section appears on the American Girl Facebook page.
The Scottsdale events will be the most recent posting, make sure to look at the correct date.
Simply hit “Join” right there on the page.
Check Facebook settings to make sure notifications are on otherwise check back on event page for live updates.
Text Message alerts will be available as well, providing updates on group numbers being admitted; details:
You may sign up for text alerts by texting AGSQ to 444222 (message and data rates may apply).
For SMS Terms and Conditions + Privacy Policy visit pocketstop.com.
You can also follow Scottsdale Quarter on Facebook at Facebook/Scottsdale Quarter
American Girl and Scottsdale Quarter are not responsible for compatibility issues or technical difficulties with technological devices.
Event staff and security officers will also be able to assist with information on what group numbers are being called.
American Girl reserves the right to stop ticket distribution at any time based on space and time frame constraints.”

posts.text:
It’s time once again for my favorite deals at the grocery stores! If you’re new to the site (WELCOME!), I put together a post of shopping secrets at all of the valley grocery stores here. If you’re new to the site, this is a GREAT place to start!
Download the Ibotta app here if you haven’t already. I LOVE IT and think everyone should have it and now Bashas takes it! Bashas even lets you redeem the deals with your Thank You Card (no receipt required). I love that you can save on many healthy items you usually can’t use coupons for. You can get money back from your purchases at grocery stores including Sprouts, Fry’s, Safeway, Whole Foods, and more (think milk, bread, bananas, broccoli, asparagus, Uncrustables, Bagel Bites, ice cream, lemons, limes, eggs, pancake mix, beer, wine, chicken, and lots more). This is a GREAT WAY to save on produce! You’ll also save at CVS Pharmacy, Target, Walmart, Walgreens, Costco, Sam’s Club, restaurants like Quizno’s, Home Depot and Lowe’s, Hallmark Stores, and more. It’s super easy to use once you get the hang of it and makes shopping way more fun. The cash back is in addition to any sales or coupons you have, and it goes right into your Paypal account (or you can get gift cards). You just redeem the offer and upload a picture of your receipt…super easy. I just got $20.80 back!
There are lots of new printable coupons. Click here to get to coupons.com and print off any coupons you think you’ll use. Save big on all kinds of things already on your list like Nissin cup noodles, Colgate Total Toothpaste, Mini Babybel cheese, Mars ice cream bars, Tide Pods, Kellogg's Special K bars, and lots more!
Don’t forget that Walmart will match any ad (with few exclusions)! You DON’T NEED THE AD! You can use this list to help you score the best prices in one spot. Head over here to find out more about their Savings Catcher program that will make sure you’re saving big! I just got $9.20 back! Get Ibotta rebates and use coupons on top of that and you’re really saving cash! I’ve heard back from so many of you who love this!
If you shop at Fry’s, head over here to load a coupon for $2 off your $40 purchase.
For even more detailed coupon match ups (I’m starting to get into doing the things I love since many of you asked), check out another great Arizona blog Bargain Believer (www.bargainbeliever.com) by my friend Juli that could save you a lot of money at the grocery store. Bashas even lets you redeem the deals with your Thank You Card (no receipt required). I love that you can save on many healthy items you usually can’t use coupons for. You can get money back from your purchases at grocery stores including Sprouts, Fry’s, Safeway, Whole Foods, and more (think green peppers, milk, lettuce, eggs, lemons, bananas, asparagus, ice cream, orange juice, onions, sugar snap peas, limes, butter, shampoo, Quaker bars, Chobani yogurt, tea, beer, wine, Tyson chicken breasts, apple juice, and lots more). It’s super easy to use once you get the hang of it and makes shopping way more fun. You just redeem the offer and upload a picture of your receipt…super easy. I just got $20.80 back!

Here's more info on cancelling:
"How do I cancel?
Just go to your orders page, which can be found in your account menu in the top right hand corner of each page on the site.
Click 'manage recurring order' or 'manage one-time order' depending on the order you wish to cancel.
Make sure you click through any subsequent options until you see confirmation of your cancellation.
If you have only one regular order set up (for example, one box that arrives every week or one box that arrives every two weeks) then this will fully cancel that regular order and no more boxes will be sent.
If you have more than one regular order set up (for example two boxes a week, or one box that gets delivered to you and one that goes to a friend) you’ll need to repeat this process for each order.
The cut-off time for making changes to your orders can be found next to ‘cut-off time’ in the middle of your deliveries page.
As long as you cancel before your cut-off time, no more boxes will be sent. If your next box is already being prepared when you cancel your regular order, then this final box will still be sent."

posts.title: Check Out the American Girl Scottsdale Grand Opening Saturday, August 22nd-Sunday, August 23rd! Free Gift for Attending (while supplies last)!

posts.text:
This is an event I KNOW a lot of girls (and their moms) are excited about! Head over here for more information about the American Girl Scottsdale grand opening event going on Saturday, August 22nd starting at 9 and Sunday, August 23rd from 11-7. Just for "joining" the event online and stopping by you'll get a free gift!
"Discover the newest American Girl store, coming soon to Scottsdale Quarter! You and your girl are invited to join in the fun during our grand-opening weekend. She’ll enjoy free crafts, exciting activities, and doll drawings, and receive a FREE gift—just for attending! Gift available while supplies last.
Please “join” this event to receive important line queue information during grand opening weekend. Ticket distribution for the grand opening is on-site and by joining this event, it does not guarantee you a place in line or entry to the store. Please visit the check-in desk upon arrival for ticket distribution."
Here's more information about how to get tickets:
"Scottsdale Quarter, Scottsdale AZ - Grand Opening
Ticket Entry Process:
To manage guests’ waiting times and observe fire-safety regulations, a ticket system will be used for the American Girl Scottsdale – Scottsdale Quarter Grand-Opening Weekend.
Each person (including children) who wishes to enter the store will receive a ticket with an assigned group number.
We recommend parking in the Scottsdale Quarter parking structures: South Garage, East entrance.
Directional signs will be visible.
American Girl guests must visit the Quad, where the fountain is located, as their first stop to obtain tickets for entrance into the store.
Ticket distribution for Saturday admittance begins at 7 a.m. on Saturday, August 22nd.
Saturday tickets are valid for Saturday only.
Ticket distribution for Sunday admittance begins at 8 a.m. on Sunday, August 23rd.
Sunday tickets are valid for Sunday only.
Overnight camping is not allowed on property.
When the store opens each day, groups will be announced in numerical order for admittance through the American Girl entrance adjacent to the main entrance on 73rd.
You can shop or dine in Scottsdale Quarter until your group number is called. If you have a Bistro reservation, you can come directly to the ticket-distribution table, as check-in is allowed up to two hours prior to your Bistro reservation time. The ticket-distribution table will be located outside the store.
Facebook message alerts will be available, providing updates on group numbers being admitted; details below.
Access the event page starting Saturday, August 22nd on your mobile device.
Once Facebook is open, search “American Girl” -
When on the page, scroll down until “Upcoming Events” section appears on the American Girl Facebook page.
The Scottsdale events will be the most recent posting, make sure to look at the correct date.
Simply hit “Join” right there on the page.
Check Facebook settings to make sure notifications are on otherwise check back on event page for live updates.
Text Message alerts will be available as well, providing updates on group numbers being admitted; details:
You may sign up for text alerts by texting AGSQ to 444222 (message and data rates may apply).
For SMS Terms and Conditions + Privacy Policy visit pocketstop.com.
You can also follow Scottsdale Quarter on Facebook at Facebook/Scottsdale Quarter
American Girl and Scottsdale Quarter are not responsible for compatibility issues or technical difficulties with technological devices.
Event staff and security officers will also be able to assist with information on what group numbers are being called.
American Girl reserves the right to stop ticket distribution at any time based on space and time frame constraints."
Enjoy!

posts.text:
Click here to snag two tickets to the Children's Museum of Phoenix for $11, a $22 value. You can choose to go August 15th-September 30th or October 1st-November 15th.
"Although classrooms can be vibrant centers for learning, they’re usually stocked with pencils and notebooks instead of a forest of suspended green noodles or a flying bathtub with wings. At the Children's Museum of Phoenix, both of these engage young minds alongside other hands-on exhibitsthat have earned the museum a glut of awards, including a place among Parents magazine’s 10 Best Children’s Museums in 2011. The museum fosters creativity and skill development in children from birth to age 10 with open-ended play activities that range from bouncing orbs in the Grand Ballroom to building forts with a wealth of safe construction materials, instead of mom’s favorite sheets and a nail gun.
Perhaps the most eye-catching feature of the museum can be found in the atrium, where the Schuff-Perini Climber soars high into the air. Created from standard building materials, found objects, and out-of-context items such as its flying bathtub, the structure entices youths and inspires their imaginations. Another impressive contraption makes up the Whoosh! exhibit, where children feed scarves into a jumble of tubes that suck the fabrics up to heights of 20 feet before spitting them out to float gently down and be caught in waiting fingers. At each of these exhibits, a baby zone keeps the tiniest museum-goers safe, and they can find a space especially for them in the Place for Threes & Younger."
Enjoy!

"The four Dillon's locations couldn't be more different. The first location, which opened in 1999, was once described as "a cute, converted old house that looks like grandma's parlor" by the Phoenix New Times. There, guests devour Kansas City–style barbecue slathered in housemade sauces and listen to live music on Fridays and Saturdays. The combination of good food and relaxed ambiance proved to be so successful that Dillon's opened a second location in Glendale in 2005. This one plays host to golfers and sports enthusiasts, entertaining them with 30 HD-TVs, as well as with live bands on the weekends.
The year 2009 saw Dillon's expanding to Scorpion Bay at Lake Pleasant, where guests can drive their boats or harnessed lochness monsters right up to the restaurant, bar, and general store and sit for a leisurely meal or grab supplies to go. In 2011, Dillon's opened perhaps its most impressive location at the Wild Life World Zoo. Here, guests can dine beside a 60,000 gallon shark tank in the dining room and vibrant pink flamingoes on the patio.
In addition to its unique settings and food, Dillon's is known for its hospitality and sense of fun, including setting up live webcams of its Scorpion Bay and zoo locations. Check them out here andhere. Dillon's particularly likes getting photos of customers enjoying the restaurants on Facebook."

Forest service rangers are on hand to point out landmarks—including the Grand Canyon, cinder-cone volcanic fields, and Sedona’s red rocks—and educate visitors about the alpine tundra beneath their feet. Passengers ages 5 and under ride free. Scenic chairlift rides operate Friday—Monday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., May 22 through mid-October.”
Heading to Prescott? Click here to get half off tickets to the Heritage Park Zoological Sanctuary.
"Heritage Park and its volunteers are dedicated to the conservation and protection of wildlife, caring for more than 150 indigenous and exotic mammals, reptiles, and birds in a 10-acre haven. Many of Heritage Park's animals were previously injured, abandoned, or marked with a human imprint that prevents them from rejoining their packs without bringing personalized coffee mugs for everyone. While prowling through the sanctuary, visitors might spy a mountain lion that was kept as a pet, a black bear that was orphaned by his mother, or a fox rescued from a swimming pool. Emus, tarantulas, and ring-tailed lemurs also run free in their habitats, serenading onlookers with their wild cries.
Heritage Park also plays an important role in the Association of Zoos & Aquariums’ Species Survival Plan, granting asylum to critically endangered Mexican gray wolves, which are being reintroduced into the wild after a 20-year absence. The zoological sanctuary is open every day, with extended hours from May 1 to October 31 to give guests a chance to see animals that are usually out running errands during business hours."

The snorkel tour explores La Jolla’s long relationship with its marine wildlife. Curious sea lions and harmless leopard sharks swim nearby as adventurers embark through a Pacific excursion. Snorkelers must be 7 or older.
For the sea-cave kayak tour, tour-goers paddle in formation behind an experienced guide and cruise through La Jolla’s local ecological preserve.
